citeAs: Conneau, A., Ma, M., Khanuja, S., Zhang, Y., Axelrod, V., Dalmia, S., Riesa, J., Rivera, C., & Bapna, A. (2022). FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech. arXiv preprint arXiv:2205.12446.
creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna (Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University)
description: FLEURS (Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech) is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language.
inLanguage: af, am, ar, hy, as, az, be, bn, bs, bg, my, ca, hr, cs, da, nl, en, et, fi, fr, ff, gl, lg, ka, de, el, gu, ha, he, hi, hu, is, ig, id, ga, it, ja, jv, kn, kk, km, ko, ky, lo, lv, ln, lt, lb, mk, ms, ml, mt, mi, mr, mn, ne, nb, ny, oc, or, om, ps, fa, pl, pt, pa, ro, ru, sr, sn, sd, sk, sl, so, es, sw, sv, tg, ta, te, th, tr, uk, ur, uz, vi, cy, wo, xh, yo, zu
name: FLEURS
rai:annotationsPerItem: Between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset (initially collected three recordings per sentence).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence in the 102 languages, three recordings were collected by three different native speakers. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded.
rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from the FLoRes-101 dataset. For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected by native speakers. Additional workers evaluated the recordings to ensure they matched the input sentence, discarding invalid ones.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All recordings are kept as they-are, either from quiet or noisy environments, without any data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For textual data: applied NFC and then FST normalization to each sentence, lower-cased, normalized and removed punctuations. Words were split into characters, and the token | was defined as word boundaries. Speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill the gaps of missing sentences (about 21.5%) in future versions of the dataset.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, enabling progress towards building speech technologies for everyone.
rai:dataUseCases: ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval.
